correctness.rationale: For each fixed number e of singleton-to-singleton maximal edges, every remaining maximal path has two endpoints in one part and a center in another. Three independent upper bounds on the triple count are proved jointly sufficient by the pair-allocation lower bounds L_i=max(0,a_i-(Q-2t)) and Hall's theorem on remaining centers. The proof handles all part sizes, integer floors, zero and complete-graph boundaries. The standalone adjacency-based brute-force verifier checked all 359 integer partitions of orders 2..13 (116315 dynamic-programming states), 990 larger constructive witnesses, and six boundary inputs. Finite computations corroborate; infinite validity rests on the Hall argument.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A complete multipartite geodesic packing is equivalently a vertex-disjoint induced P3 packing together with singleton-class edges, so these terms were searched rather than checking titles alone. General induced-path complexity theorems and generic packing language neither give exact heterogeneous values nor the mixed-type feasibility criterion. The 1996 induced-path partition number is not a dominating scalar: K_{2,1,1,1,1,1} and K_{3,3,1} each have seven vertices and induced-path partition number three, but their geodesic packing numbers are respectively three and two (direct explicit witnesses and capacity upper bound).

originality.rationale: The 2022 originating geodesic-packing paper supplies only the complete-graph and balanced-complete-bipartite special cases among complete multipartite graphs. An earlier geodesic-transversal result treats hitting, not packing. A 2019 paper on multipartite pansophy concerns expected routing of randomly assigned terminal pairs, not maximal shortest-path packings. Published-research and literature searches did not find an equivalent heterogeneous three-capacity packing criterion. Residual risk remains for older equivalent induced-path tilings under alternate terms.
residual_risks: Older induced-three-vertex-path factor or path-tiling literature may contain an equivalent result not indexed under geodesic-packing terminology.

The 1996 Broere–Jonck–Voigt source is closely related but optimizes a minimum induced-path partition, not maximal geodesic packing. Its complete full text could not be retrieved from the accessible author-upload link; overlap through an ancillary theorem in its uninspected text remains a bounded risk.

value.rationale: Determines a natural NP-hard graph invariant in polynomial time over every connected complete multipartite graph. The exact (e,t)-feasibility region and Hall construction are structural, not just a renamed bound; both singleton-to-singleton maximal edges and three-vertex paths are indispensable (e.g. K_{2,1,1,1,1,1}). The result unifies and extends the known complete graph and balanced-biclique examples without claiming those as novel; it gives reusable capacity criteria for disjoint-geodesic resource allocation.
